name: Sudip Paudel
headline: I write the layer most people import.
summary: Register-level firmware on ARM Cortex-M4, synthesised SystemVerilog on FPGA, and two platforms running in production. Computer Engineering at UT Arlington.
about: Most of my work happens a layer below where people usually start.

On the TM4C123 I write the clock, UART, timer and NVIC setup myself, straight out of the datasheet, rather than calling TI's HAL. It takes much longer to get anything working. It also means that when something breaks I know which register I got wrong. FPGA work runs on the same instinct in SystemVerilog: I pay more attention to the timing report than the simulation waveform, because a design can simulate perfectly and still fail to close.

I write web software too. AntarLens and Kashlly are both live, and I built each one end to end: schema, auth, the product, the deploy. On AntarLens the user isolation lives in Postgres row-level security instead of route handlers, so a bug in my own code can't hand one person's data to somebody else.
I'm at UT Arlington studying Computer Engineering. Open to internships or roles close to the hardware, the systems, or both.
